verdict.rationale: Trivy's filesystem docs show it scans local projects for vulnerabilities using lock files, naming Gemfile.lock (Ruby) and package-lock.json (npm), and it can generate SBOMs for local projects. This confirms multi-ecosystem project scanning, but the evidence names only two ecosystems and gives no full language or package-manager support matrix. Missing for 10: a documented list of supported languages and package managers (e.g. Python, Java, Go, .NET, Rust, PHP), detail on detection accuracy per ecosystem, and independent hands-on corroboration of broad language coverage.

support.subject: As a developer, I can scan projects across all the major languages and package ecosystems my organization uses

citations.quote: Trivy will look for vulnerabilities based on lock files such as Gemfile.lock and package-lock.json.
Trivy can generate SBOM for local projects.
It detects known vulnerabilities in your container image.
